scope: New PRL-oriented Cartesian axes, subplots, insets, and colorbars unless a user explicitly requests another direction.
recommendation: Set major and minor ticks inward and inspect the rendered result for special projections.
counterexamples: Special projections or an explicit user override may require another direction.
limitations: This is a configurable local default, not an APS requirement and not a corpus frequency claim.

scope: Figure canvases delivered by this skill when the user has not explicitly requested explanatory text inside the image.
recommendation: Move method summaries, caveats, fit statistics, provenance, and result commentary to the separate caption or manuscript.
counterexamples: An explicit user request can authorize explanatory on-image text; essential axes, legends, colorbars, panel IDs, scale bars, and schematic labels remain readable.
limitations: This is a local legibility and evidence-separation rule, not an official PRL mandate; the semantic role of each text artist still requires review.

scope: Adapting a reviewed reference figure or a recipe to user data.
recommendation: Preserve the referents, quantity identity, normalization, uncertainty meaning, and full-view context that the source makes necessary; do not treat visual similarity as scientific validation.
counterexamples: A user may choose a different encoding when the supplied data or accessibility requirement makes it clearer.
limitations: This workflow rule protects meaning and provenance; it does not claim that every PRL figure uses the same composition.

scope: The accepted calibration review of the cited comparison figure; use as a design prompt when the same visual roles occur, not as a frequency or journal rule.
recommendation: When color and marker or line-style encodings distinguish comparison roles, retain an explicit mapping in the adapted legend or caption and verify it in the final export.
counterexamples: A single reviewed comparison figure cannot establish that redundant encodings are required in all PRL figures.
limitations: One accepted agent visual review records visible color, marker, and line-style observations; it does not establish font identity, scientific validity, prevalence, or accessibility compliance.

scope: All style-distillation observations whose source region is raster-only or whose PDF text layer is absent.
recommendation: Record font identity as not_measurable and keep typography defaults sourced from vector text evidence or explicit local configuration; never infer a font family from raster appearance alone.
limitations: None are promoted as universal counterexamples because no accepted visual review support is available; this card documents a measurement boundary and keeps raster limitations explicit.
